what_it_does: Automotive radar must simultaneously detect distant vehicles (long-range), nearby obstacles (short-range), and measure both distance and angle with good precision. Current phased-array radars optimize for either range or resolution but struggle to do both well. This paper presents a fully integrated 77-gigahertz radar system with 8 transmitters and 8 receivers that dynamically switches between three operating modes (long-range, medium-range, short-range) by changing the chirp pattern (the frequency sweep used in FM radar). The system combines TDMA (time-division: transmitters take turns) with MIMO beamforming (multiple transmitters and receivers creating virtual antenna arrays) to achieve 186-meter detection range and 3-centimeter distance resolution.
